Q: How to unescape HTML entities in python A:

Its easier to use a regex to match the name or code number, then do a replacement:
Sample Python using a callback to do the replacement..

https://www.online-python.com/sF5CuaP4ck Decimal int name hash ( Current )
https://www.online-python.com/BSPtuYqDxs Hex string name hash initialization ( Previous )

import re

def repl(m):
    t = m.group(3)
    if m.group(1) :
        return chr(int(t,16)) if m.group(2) else chr(int(t))
    return chr(ent_names[t]) if t in ent_names else m.group()

def main():
    test_str = ('Hello  𝓏  ‍  ‌  < ♦ ¨  ⋄  ♦ > ' '
                ' ¥ € ' &unknown; > World')
    mod_str = re.sub(r'(?i)(?=&(?:[a-z]+|\#(?:[0-9]+|x[0-9a-f]+));)&(\#)?(x)?([0-9a-z]+);', repl, test_str )
    print ( test_str + "\n" + mod_str + "\n" )

Q: Lowest common ancestor C++ A: 
findLCA(const T& n1, const T& n2) {

You are making a lot of assumptions here, but you do not check that the assumptions are correct.

For example, what is curr? Perhaps it does not point to a node? What if it points to a child of the node that contains n1 or n2. What if it is null - then your app will crash at ( Actually, your compiler should flag this - if it doesn't then you need a better compiler )

Another example: You are assuming that the data contained by any node is always unique, and that n1 and n2 are present, somewhere in the tree.

Usually, a method to find the LCA is passed the nodes, not the data values from which unique nodes may or may not be found.

=========================

You have not shown us your code for the class BST. It should have an attribute that points to the root of the tree. Get rid of curr and start from the root. Now search down through the tree to find the node that contains n1 and n2. Keep a record of the paths, which will give you the node where they diverge - i.e. the LCA
